title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on the May 12th reliability incident (timeouts / 5xxs). Reviewed logs, root-cause hypotheses (burst traffic + KV cache eviction), mitigation steps (retry/backoff tuning, circuit breaker, rate-limit bump), and agreed next steps: collect full traces, run controlled repro, schedule SE deep-dive and update SOC2/security docs for procurement thread.
transcript: [00:00] Samir Patel: Hey team, thanks for joining the weekly. we know there's a short agenda, main item is the incident from May 12 — follow up on root cause and next steps.
[00:18] Maya Lopez: Yep thanks Samir. we're still seeing intermittent timeouts in prod - mostly 504s for the /generate route. Tom is on the line to share what he's seen.

[00:33] Tom Reynolds: hi all. quick context, we saw a burst around 14:12 UTC, a spike of concurrent sessions hitting our inference endpoints, roughly 3x normal. about 2-3% of requests returned 5xx, and a handful were 524-ish timeouts from the load balancer. we captured some logs and traces.
[00:50] Alex Chen: do you have the request patterns? e.g., sequence length, batch sizes, or any sudden change in prefix distribution? those can affect memory and kernel selection.
[01:05] Priya Singh: mostly short prompts, average 120 tokens, but a subset of tests were longer — up to 1.2k tokens for evaluation runs. we didn't change client batching intentionally.
[01:22] Tom Reynolds: interestingly, KV cache evictions show up in the logs — lots of mem pressure warnings. also we saw a couple of OOM-ish hints from the runtime, but not full node crashes.

[01:38] Samir Patel: ok that aligns with a capacity transient. Alex, is that consistent with Redwood runtime behaviour when you mix long sequences with short ones? any kernel / quantization interactions?

[01:54] Alex Chen: yeah, mixing long and short can force a less-optimized kernel path for a subset of shards. plus when KV cache grows it increases memory usage — and if a lot of sessions open, the KV cache can be evicted, causing retries and spikes. also sometimes the autoscaler takes a bit to spin up GPUs if config is tuned conservative.
[02:10] Maya Lopez: we were on dedicated pool but with autoscaling min=2, max=6; at the time we were sitting at 2 and then hit the spike. is there a way to set burst capacity or faster scale-up?

[02:27] Alex Chen: yes, there are two levers: short-term we can request a temporary burst increase (reserve extra capacity) and increase the autoscaler aggressiveness; longer term we recommend prefix caching and request shaping so the sudden fan-out doesn't push mem beyond node limits.
[02:45] Tom Reynolds: one question: some of our clients hit the endpoint with heavy retry logic that does linear retry with no jitter. that likely worsened the spike. any recommendations?

[03:00] Samir Patel: good callout. best practice is exponential backoff with jitter and a capped retry count; Redwood SDKs have retry helpers but client-side tuning is critical — we can share sample code.
[03:18] Priya Singh: the load balancer timeouts were 60s, and some requests were queued. is there any way to make the runtime respond faster under memory pressure?

[03:32] Alex Chen: when memory pressure is high, latency SLOs slip because of device-to-host transfers or kernel fallbacks. we can enable partial response streaming earlier or configure an early circuit-breaker to fail fast and let client retry with backoff. that avoids piling on.

[03:50] Tom Reynolds: we noticed many of the 5xx errors were 503 with message that looked like "model unavailable" — though the model was still serving. transcription might show "model unavailble" in our logs due to truncated messages.
[04:05] Maya Lopez: also curious about rate-limits — were we hitting a per-tenant throttle? our app has per-user bursts.

[04:18] Alex Chen: Redwood has multi-tier rate limiting: route level, tenant level, and pod level. the POC default is conservative. we can temporarily raise tenant limits for your demo window. we also recommend smoothing bursts at the client or using a local queue.
[04:35] Priya Singh: can you explain the KV cache eviction note — we saw logs saying "k v cache evicted: session 1234" and then retries.

[04:50] Alex Chen: kv cache eviction happens when overall KV memory used by cached prefixes exceeds the configured cache budget. eviction forces recomputation or reloads which spikes CPU/GPU usage while repopulating — that combined with incoming new requests can exceed capacity.

[05:07] Samir Patel: ok sounds like the short-term mitigation is: 1) bump tenant rate limit for a 24-48h window, 2) adjust autoscaler policy for faster scale-up, and 3) share client-side retry best-practices. we'll add longer-term items too.

[05:25] Tom Reynolds: we already have logs and a few spans — I'll upload traces to the shared S3 link you gave earlier. link: s3://bluewave-poc/traces/2026-05-12/. some trace ids: trc-7a2e, trc-7a2f. they might be redacted but should help.
[05:42] Alex Chen: perfect. can you also share a sample request (prompt + headers) that hit the long-run path? that helps us repro locally.
[05:55] Maya Lopez: yes will share. also, for the audit team, they asked about encrypted logs and whether KMS keys are customer-managed in Private deploys. not urgent but part of procurement.

[06:12] Samir Patel: noted — we'll attach the SOC 2 / encryption docs. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS in our Private offering; for Dedicated we provide options too — I'll include detail in the follow-up.
[06:28] Priya Singh: rough timeline — we're aiming for production cutover by Q3. this incident concerns stakeholders; hoping we can close mitigation this week.
[06:40] Alex Chen: for a quick repro, we can simulate the mixed workload and KV pressure in our staging. if you can provide a replay file we can run it and surface the kernel traces.
[06:55] Tom Reynolds: I'll package the replay by EOD tomorrow. also question on metrics — can Redwood surface per-session KV cache size and eviction counts?
[07:08] Alex Chen: yes, we can emit eviction_count, kv_cache_bytes, and per-model mem usage to your observability sink. we support Prometheus scraping or pushing to your Grafana Cloud.
[07:23] Maya Lopez: that would be ideal. currently we only have high-level latency and error rates, not the internal runtime metrics.

[07:35] Samir Patel: action wise, let's enumerate: collect traces (Tom), provide replay (Tom + Priya), Redwood to run repro and surface kernel traces (Alex), request temporary rate-limit bump and autoscaler tweak (Samir), and share SOC2 + KMS docs (Samir).
[07:55] Priya Singh: can we also get a recommended retry/backoff snippet? our client library has a homegrown approach.

[08:08] Alex Chen: yes — we'll send a snippet with exponential backoff + jitter and a recommended max retries of 3 for generation endpoints. also example for streaming where you can fallback to partial content.
[08:22] Tom Reynolds: about retries — we saw a loop where clients retried immediately which doubled the load — not good. adding jitter helped in other systems.
[08:35] Samir Patel: another mitigation: set soft per-session QPS caps on the proxy layer so a single user can't spike the cluster.
[08:47] Maya Lopez: any concern about quality regressions if you change kernel selection or quantization profiles to reduce memory? we don't want hallucination regressions.

[09:02] Alex Chen: good point. kernel selection normally doesn't change model outputs, but quantization can affect numeric fidelity. for safety we'll avoid aggressive quantization for your eval models; instead we suggest routing long evaluations to a higher-memory pool.
[09:20] Priya Singh: what about checking request idempotency? some of the client workflows are not idempotent and retries produced duplicated downstream writes.
[09:33] Samir Patel: that's a client-side constraint; we can recommend idempotency keys and best practices in the deck we share.
[09:47] Tom Reynolds: any immediate logs we should grep for when we upload traces? specific error codes or markers?
[09:58] Alex Chen: search for "kv_cache_evicted", "alloc_failure", "kernel_fallback", and 503/504 in the runtime logs. also include the model-version header so we can match kernel profiles.
[10:14] Maya Lopez: ok we'll include those. schedule wise, can we do the repro run on Thursday? that gives us time to collect and sanitize traces.
[10:26] Alex Chen: Thursday works, Alex (SE) can run a repro and share results in the deep-dive. I can also prepare a short doc on autoscaler and caching knobs.

[10:39] Samir Patel: one more internal ask: procurement has asked for an SLA note on availability during POC. our hosted offering has standard terms but for Dedicated we can provide targets; I'll attach language.
[10:54] Priya Singh: great — procurement will also want a statement about data residency; BlueWave processes EU patient metadata, so this matters.
[11:06] Samir Patel: noted — we'll include data residency+audit options for Dedicated/Private in the follow-up. Private supports VPC + on-prem.
[11:19] Tom Reynolds: curious about circuit-breaker patterns — does Redwood runtime expose a circuit-breaker config we can tweak?

[11:30] Alex Chen: we have both runtime and gateway-level circuit breakers. runtime level can return 429/503 fast if queue depth exceeds threshold; gateway-level can be configured to shed load earlier. we'll propose conservative thresholds for your traffic pattern.
[11:48] Maya Lopez: okay, sounds like a plan. any blockers from Redwood side to start the repro?
[11:56] Alex Chen: just the replay and traces from you; and confirmation to bump tenant limit for the test window. we'll need an owner to approve the temporary limit increase.
[12:09] Samir Patel: I'll raise it internally and send a one-off tenant limit increase for 48 hours once Tom signs off. we'll cc procurement on the SOC2 docs.
[12:22] Priya Singh: Tom will sign off. Tom — can you confirm by EOD?
[12:28] Tom Reynolds: yes I'll confirm EOD, and upload the replay by tomorrow evening.
[12:35] Samir Patel: cool. quick recap and next steps before we close?

[12:42] Samir Patel: recap: (1) Tom to upload traces & replay (due 2026-05-15), (2) Alex to run repro & surface kernel traces (target 2026-05-21), (3) Samir to request 48h tenant limit bump and share SOC2/KMS docs (due 2026-05-16), (4) Redwood to provide retry snippet and autoscaler/caching docs (due 2026-05-16), (5) schedule deep-dive if repro shows kernel fallback (tentative 2026-05-22).
[13:08] Priya Singh: that looks right. one more ask: can you also provide a short risk statement we can share with execs about the incident and mitigation?
[13:18] Samir Patel: yes we'll put together a 1-page risk summary and share.
[13:26] Maya Lopez: thanks everyone. appreciate the quick response. any final comments?
[13:33] Alex Chen: just to reiterate, enabled metrics and eviction counts will help a lot — we'll add those exports as part of the repro job.
[13:43] Tom Reynolds: thanks all. logging out after I upload the artifacts.
[13:50] Samir Patel: thanks team. we'll follow up in email with attachments and the tenant bump request. bye.
[13:56] (meeting ends)
Notes: transcript contains small transcription errors; product names sometimes mispelled (e.g., "K-V cash"), timestamps approximate.
